newsitem.title: UK: TI slips further after analysts meeting.
newsitem.headline: TI slips further after analysts meeting.

text.p: Shares in engineering group TI Group Plc extended earlier losses on Thursday following an analysts briefing on the company's first-half results and after SocGen recommended "taking profits", noting it planned to cut earnings estimates.
The shares were off 29p to 540p by 1120 GMT after initially falling around 19p following the results.
Zafar Khan, engineering analyst at SocGen recommended taking profits after the shares climbed 55p the previous two days on the back of weakness in the pound.
"The shares look reasonably fairly valued at this level, we don't see the stock outperforming from here," he said.

"We may see some trimming of forecasts to around the 230 million stg level," Khan said, adding he would probably revise his own forecast down slightly to take account of disappointment in the seals business and to factor in estimated currency effects.

TI earlier announced profits above average forecasts. Analysts said the aerospace business had done better than expected but the seals division was still struggling. The impact from the strength of the pound, at 7.6 million stg provided no major shock.
Khan said he was encouraged by an 11 percent increase in the order books and described the company's performance as "steady".
The company said the anticipated currency impact in the second half was 7-10 million stg, broadly in line with analysts expectations.
